tasks.spec:
You work in the MAIN checkout of the game repo: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (not a worktree; it holds many uncommitted changes that belong to other work and MUST stay untouched). FIRST run `cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge`. NEVER git commit, git stash, git checkout/restore/reset, never `uv`, never call a billed model or the network, never run `python -m bench run`, `python -m bench.frozen_prompts replay` or any script that calls a model. Run tests as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <tests>`. Ruff: `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files>` and `-m ruff format <files>`. Do not edit any file except those listed under OWNERSHIP.

BACKGROUND. The narrator prompt lists, per speaker, what that character may say aloud: storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py `_speaker_constraint_lines` renders `<Name> may say this aloud: <statement>` using the canonical third-person `statement` of each sayable knowledge entry (items come from `_speaker_context`, around line 2139, as {"id", "statement"} per speaker). A third-person statement about the speaker herself (e.g. Michelle told to say "Michelle coordinates the prisoners") makes the small narrator model produce self-reference in the third person. Brandon wants each speaker's sayable line AUTHORED in advance in that speaker's own voice. This task adds that authoring field. It adds NO prompt sentence.

DESIGN (follow exactly).
1. Model. In storygame/story_package/models.py add to `KnowledgeDefinition` an optional field `speaker_text`: a mapping from character id to the words that character may say aloud for this entry. Authored YAML form: a mapping `speaker_id: "text"`. Choose a frozen/immutable representation consistent with the other models in that file (it must not break equality or hashing that other models rely on). It is omitted from serialization (model_dump / JSON / package fingerprint) when empty, exactly like `voiceable` and `delivery_variants` use `exclude_if`, so every existing package serializes byte-for-byte as before. Reject at load: a blank/whitespace-only value, a non-string value, a non-string or malformed key, and a non-empty map on an entry with `voiceable: false` (contradictory authoring).
2. Package validation. In storygame/story_package/loader.py, next to where `reach_entity_ids` are checked against known entities, reject a speaker id that is not a declared character/NPC of the package world (raise StoryPackageError with the knowledge id and the unknown id, same style as the neighbouring checks). The protagonist is not a speaker.
3. Rendering. `speaker_text` is presentation only: it never changes the canonical `statement`, facts, eligibility, grounding, leak/safety checks, SCENE text, the `brought_up` list or `ProjectedKnowledge`. In cloudflare.py, where `_speaker_context` builds each speaker's sayable items, look the entry up by id in `self.state.package.knowledge.knowledge` and, ONLY for that speaker, add the speaker's own text to the item dict (for example key "spoken"); `_speaker_constraint_lines` then renders `<Name> may say this aloud: <spoken>` INSTEAD of the statement (one line, never both). Rules: (a) entry with no `speaker_text` at all: unchanged rendering with the statement; (b) entry with a non-empty map and this speaker listed: the speaker's text; (c) entry with a non-empty map and this speaker NOT listed: that speaker gets NO speakable line for the entry (a speaker never falls back to a third-person statement that may describe themselves; the knowledge stays in the committed/SCENE material). The mapping as a whole, and another speaker's text, must never appear in a speaker's context. Line order, count and format are otherwise unchanged. Everything else in cloudflare.py stays as is; check that the opening, normal-turn and recovery paths all build lines through this one helper (recovery reuses the original payload).
4. Story data. In data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml add `speaker_text` (key placed right after `delivery_text`) to exactly these four entries, with EXACTLY this text (Brandon approved the wording; do not edit, re-punctuate or add entries):
  k_sl_3a_a_r1:
    michelle: "I've been organizing everyone with secret announcements over our stolen radios."
    brandon: "Dr. McGehee's been organizing everyone with secret announcements over the stolen radios."
    senior_official: "Dr. McGehee's been organizing everyone with secret announcements over the stolen radios."
  k_sl_3a_b_r2:
    michelle: "I showed you the medical level. That's where they ran memory, compliance, and resistance experiments on the prisoners."
    brandon: "Dr. McGehee showed you the medical level. That's where they ran memory, compliance, and resistance experiments on the prisoners."
    senior_official: "Dr. McGehee showed you the medical level. That's where they ran memory, compliance, and resistance experiments on the prisoners."
  k_sl_3a_d_r1:
    michelle: "The official Charles framed gave you one-use authorization for the emergency surface gates. It expires when Charles activates his new authority."
    brandon: "The official Charles framed gave you one-use authorization for the emergency surface gates. It expires when Charles activates his new authority."
    senior_official: "I gave you one-use authorization for the emergency surface gates. It expires when Charles activates his new authority."
  k_sl_3a_c_r1:
    michelle: "I gave you the radio, you gave the signal, and now the prisoners have the checkpoints and are fighting their way up toward the command and broadcast levels."
    brandon: "Dr. McGehee gave you the radio, you gave the signal, and now the prisoners have the checkpoints and are fighting their way up toward the command and broadcast levels."
    senior_official: "Dr. McGehee gave you the radio, you gave the signal, and now the prisoners have the checkpoints and are fighting their way up toward the command and broadcast levels."
   No other entry, statement, fact, delivery_text or file of the story changes. The speaker ids are michelle, brandon, senior_official.

TESTS FIRST. Before touching any non-test file, write tests/test_speaker_text.py and run it to see it fail for the right reason (record the failing summary in your final notes). Read tests/test_speaker_lines.py, tests/test_cloudflare_transport.py and tests/test_voiceable_knowledge.py first and copy their fixtures; build states the same way they do (real ItemFactsProvider subclass used by those tests, no network, no model). Required tests: (a) model: absent field is absent from serialization of an existing definition and an unchanged package fingerprint/dump for a package with no speaker_text; valid map accepted; blank value, non-string value, and speaker_text with voiceable false each rejected. (b) loader: unknown speaker id rejected with a clear error; a declared character accepted. (c) rendering through the real provider: entry without speaker_text renders the statement as before; with a map, each listed speaker's line contains only that speaker's text and not the canonical statement and not another speaker's text; a present speaker not listed in a non-empty map gets no line for that entry while another listed speaker does; line count and order otherwise unchanged; a speaker's request payload never contains another speaker's text. (d) the real continuity-initiative package: the four entries carry exactly the approved texts per speaker (assert the full strings), and no other knowledge entry has speaker_text. (e) canonical `statement` for the four entries is unchanged and SCENE/brought_up still use it. Then implement the minimum code and make them pass.

EXISTING TESTS. Run the related suites (list in the check). If a test fails only because it pins the old text of those four sayable lines, the package fingerprint, or the model field list, update just the pinned expectation, keep the test's intent, never delete or weaken a test, never loosen a rule. In your final notes list every existing test file you changed and why. If something else fails, stop and report it rather than working around it.

PAYLOAD MATCH (the acceptance test). After the work, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python scripts/ringer/shared-narrator/gu_match.py` must print MATCH for system and user at c4, c5 and c9 (it compares the real engine payloads, with the gate that is already in the tree, against the frozen experiment arm). Do not edit that script or anything under bench/ or scripts/.

OWNERSHIP. You may create or edit only: storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py, data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml, tests/test_speaker_text.py, and existing files under tests/ whose pinned expectations change as described above. Leave all changes uncommitted in place.
